items.stem: Carbon forms covalent bonds because:
items.answer: it cannot easily gain or lose four electrons

items.stem: What type of covalent bond(s) does a molecule of propane (C₃H₈) contain?
items.markingKey: (b) Propane: 10 single bonds.

items.stem: Why is diamond hard but graphite soft and slippery?
items.answer: In diamond each carbon is bonded to four others in a rigid 3-D network; in graphite each carbon is bonded to three others in layers that slide over each other.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: How many covalent bonds are present in a molecule of carbon dioxide (CO₂), and how many electrons are shared in all?
items.markingKey: Single = 2 electrons, double = 4, triple = 6: 2 double = 8 electrons.

items.stem: How many covalent bonds are present in a molecule of ethene (C₂H₄), and how many electrons are shared in all?
items.markingKey: Single = 2 electrons, double = 4, triple = 6: 4 single, 1 double = 12 electrons.

items.stem: How many covalent bonds are present in a molecule of chlorine (Cl₂), and how many electrons are shared in all?
items.markingKey: Single = 2 electrons, double = 4, triple = 6: 1 single = 2 electrons.

items.stem: How many covalent bonds are present in a molecule of ammonia (NH₃), and how many electrons are shared in all?
items.markingKey: Single = 2 electrons, double = 4, triple = 6: 3 single = 6 electrons.

items.stem: Why does a mixture of ethyne and oxygen, rather than ethyne and air, give a hot enough flame for welding?
items.answer: With pure oxygen, ethyne burns completely and releases more heat quickly; air has only about 21% oxygen, so combustion is incomplete and a sooty, cooler flame forms.
items.markingKey: 1 mark complete combustion. 1 mark air has less O₂. 1 mark sooty flame.

items.stem: What type of covalent bond(s) does a molecule of water (H₂O) contain?
items.markingKey: (a) Water: 2 single bonds.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A covalent bond formed by sharing three pairs of electrons."
items.markingKey: (d) A triple bond is a covalent bond formed by sharing three pairs of electrons.

items.stem: What is meant by tetravalency?
items.answer: The property of carbon of having a valency of four

items.stem: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
items.markingKey: (b) Cyclohexane is a saturated hydrocarbon. The others: benzene – an unsaturated hydrocarbon; ethene – an unsaturated hydrocarbon; propene – an unsaturated hydrocarbon.

items.stem: Give two differences between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons.
items.answer: Saturated: only single bonds, burn with a clean blue flame. Unsaturated: double or triple bonds, burn with a yellow sooty flame and undergo addition reactions.

items.stem: Assuming an open-chain hydrocarbon, is C₃H₈ saturated or unsaturated? Which homologous series does it belong to?

items.stem: Classify these as an unsaturated hydrocarbon or a saturated hydrocarbon: ethane, butane, ethyne, cyclohexane, propene.
items.answer: An unsaturated hydrocarbon: ethyne, propene. A saturated hydrocarbon: butane, cyclohexane, ethane.

items.stem:
Read: A refinery in Mathura separates hydrocarbons. Sample P is butane and sample Q is butene. Q decolourises bromine water; P does not.
(i) Write the molecular formulae of P and Q. (ii) Which is saturated? (iii) Why does Q decolourise bromine water? (iv) What will be formed when Q is treated with hydrogen in the presence of nickel?
items.answer: (i) P: C₄H₁₀; Q: C₄H₈. (ii) P (butane). (iii) It has a C=C double bond and undergoes an addition reaction. (iv) butane (C₄H₁₀).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Why does the bottom of a cooking vessel get blackened when the gas burner flame is yellow?
items.answer: The air holes are blocked, so the fuel burns incompletely and unburnt carbon (soot) deposits on the vessel.

items.stem: A student adds soap to water from a borewell in Gurugram and gets little lather but a lot of curdy precipitate. Explain and suggest two remedies.
items.answer: The water is hard (Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ salts); soap reacts to form insoluble scum. Use a detergent, or soften the water by boiling or adding washing soda.
items.markingKey: 1 mark hard water. 1 mark scum. 1 mark remedies.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A cluster of soap molecules in water with the hydrocarbon tails inside and ionic heads outside."
items.markingKey: (b) A micelle is a cluster of soap molecules in water with the hydrocarbon tails inside and ionic heads outside.

items.stem: What are soaps and detergents? Explain the formation of micelles and the cleansing action of soap with a diagram. Why do soaps not work well in hard water?
items.answer: Soaps: sodium or potassium salts of long-chain carboxylic acids; detergents: ammonium or sulphonate salts of long-chain acids. Soap molecule: ionic hydrophilic head, hydrocarbon hydrophobic tail; in water tails point inward into oil, heads outward, forming a micelle that is rinsed away. Hard water Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ form insoluble scum with soap.
items.markingKey: 1 mark definitions; 3 marks micelle and cleansing; 1 mark hard water.
